key_insight: V-PaSS improves perovskite solar-cell prediction by encoding absorber mixtures and device stacks with physics-aware, semantically rich representations that can generalize to unseen materials and architectures.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable screening of novel perovskite compositions and stack designs before fabrication, reducing costly trial-and-error in solar-cell development.
method: Interpolates relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX3 endmembers using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing to represent mixed-cation/mixed-halide absorbers.
Encodes the device stack with layer order, polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n), and interfacial band offsets.
Uses a scientific language model to capture chemical descriptions beyond simple categorical labels.
evidence_signal: Under an institution-grouped evaluation where test devices came from unseen laboratories, V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE, beating the best tuned benchmark (2.912%) and a gradient-boosted baseline (3.017%), with larger gains on unseen alloys and transport layers.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable endpoint crystal data and physical assumptions like Vegard interpolation and bandgap bowing, which may be less accurate for highly nonideal or poorly characterized alloys.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
